name: NuVIE
attribution: NuVIE is a fictional streaming companion app invented for this concept study, and the name, brand, research, flows, and screens are entirely my own work. The streaming service logos that appear inside the mockups belong to their respective owners and indicate where a title could be watched, nothing more.
dek: A watch-tracking app built around deciding what to watch next.

at_a_glance.role: Sole UX/UI designer, end to end
at_a_glance.scope: Competitor analysis, user flows, design system, hi-fi UI, usability test plan
at_a_glance.hard_part: Turning an open-ended catalog into a short guided path, so a person with decision fatigue lands on one confident pick instead of endless scrolling.
at_a_glance.look_for: How the mode picker, the onboarding genre step, and the questionnaire components all push toward the same goal: fewer options on screen at any moment.

problem.claim_h2: The problem is not finding movies. It is choosing one.
problem.thesis: Tracking apps tell you where a title streams, but none of them help you decide what to actually watch tonight.
problem.body: A review of Reelgood, JustWatch, Trakt, and IMDb-style recommendation feeds showed the same pattern: passive lists, generic suggestions, and walls of options that make the choice harder. NuVIE reframes the tracker as a decision tool, pairing watchlists and streaming availability with a short mood-based questionnaire.
bullets: Recommendations are trend-driven rather than mood-driven, so they feel generic and impersonal.
Availability tools answer where to watch but leave the harder what-to-watch question open.
Oversized catalogs and cluttered layouts overwhelm exactly the users who want a quick answer.
problem.research_note: A competitor teardown of IMDb, JustWatch, Reelgood, and Trakt compared watchlist handling, streaming info, and recommendation style to locate the gap NuVIE fills.

design.claim_h2: A guided path from mood to one good pick
design.intro: Read this chapter as flow and system work rather than finished content. The mode picker, the onboarding order, and the component sheet define how a person would move from a mood to a short list, while several downstream screens in the source file still hold placeholder posters and copy, so the argument here lives in the structure of the path, not in polished surfaces.

figures.caption: The mode picker leads with occasions, Movie Night or Binge Week, so the first choice is about intent, not titles.
figures.alt: Phone on a dark desk showing NuVIE's orange mode-select screen with Movie Night and Binge Week buttons plus Quick Mode and Advanced Mode options.

figures.caption: Onboarding runs login, social signup, a favorite genre step, then a confirmation screen. The genre tiles are unlabeled placeholders at concept fidelity, and what the flow commits to is the order: taste capture before the home feed ever loads.
figures.alt: Four orange NuVIE onboarding screens: a login form, a signup screen with Google, Facebook and Apple buttons, a genre picker made of blank placeholder circles, and a confirmation screen with a Next button.

validation.claim_h2: How I planned to put it in front of people
validation.honest_line: Walking a participant through these tasks could show whether the mode picker reads as the start of the journey, whether the questionnaire feels faster than browsing a feed, and whether the folder structure for saved titles is discoverable. It could not show whether guided picks actually beat open scrolling over time, and because the catalog screens hold placeholder posters, it could not test how real cover art would shape the choice.
validation.limit_line: What stands here is a plan for sessions that never took place: no participant has used NuVIE, and none of these screens has been checked against live behavior.

appendix.framing: Selected system artifacts behind the screens. The component sheet shows the questionnaire and navigation states that carry the guided flow.

figures.caption: Empty and selected states for answer cards, five nav-bar states, and streaming-platform cards define the questionnaire's building blocks.
figures.alt: Component sheet showing navigation bar variants, toggles, question cards in empty and selected states, keyboards, and streaming platform logo cards.
